heading: 1. Log in
text: 1. Log in Exchange your username and password for a token (form encoded, not JSON). curl -X POST https://app.raghim.com/api/token \ -d "username=you@example.com" -d "password=YOUR_PASSWORD" # {"access_token": "eyJ...", "token_type": "bearer"} Accounts with 2FA enabled receive a challenge response instead and need the extra verification step first. For long-lived automation use an access token with the MCP endpoint rather than storing a password.

heading: 2. Upload a document
text: 2. Upload a document curl -X POST https://app.raghim.com/api/documents/upload/background \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ -F "files=@handbook.pdf" \ -F "collection_name=my-docs" Processing runs in the background (chunking, embedding). Wait until the document shows as processed in the app before asking questions about it.

heading: 3. Ask a question
text: 3. Ask a question curl -X POST https://app.raghim.com/api/chat/agentic \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"message": "What is our refund policy?", "collections": ["my-docs"]}' # {"response": "...", "sources": [...]} The answer comes back in response , with the passages it used in sources . Using Claude, Cursor or another AI client? Skip the raw API and connect through MCP: MCP setup . Next MCP Setup

heading: 1. Pick a starting point
text: 1. Pick a starting point Open Flows and choose New from template . Good first choices: Knowledge assistant: Start, document search, answer, End. Ideal for an internal wiki or HR questions. Data analyst: Start, database query, answer, End. For tables and summaries without documents. Blank: only Start and End, for building from scratch. Prefer to describe it? Use Generate flow draft from the More (⋮) menu, write what you want in a sentence or two, and click Generate . The draft is saved but not live, so you can review it first.

heading: 2. Adjust the steps
text: 2. Adjust the steps Use + Tool to add things the flow can do (document search, SQL, MCP tools) and + Logic for guardrails and decisions. Click a step to set it up. For a document search step, you must select the collections it may use. A flow needs exactly one Start node, and every step must be connected.

heading: 3. Test before you go live
text: 3. Test before you go live Save the flow, then send a test message in Preview . You will see the agent's reply and can open each step's output to see what it did. Fix anything odd before deploying.

heading: 4. Deploy
text: 4. Deploy Click Deploy (you must save first). Once deployed, the Agent and your widgets use this flow. You can also turn on failure alerts, which email you if the flow fails repeatedly, and share a flow with your organization. Safe by design: editing and drafting never make a flow live. Only a person pressing Deploy does, including when you build flows from an AI assistant over MCP .

heading: 1. Create an access token
text: 1. Create an access token In Raghim open Security Settings → MCP access tokens , name the token, pick scopes and an expiry, and copy it. It starts with rgh_ and is shown once . Tokens belong to you, carry your organization and role, and can be revoked at any time. read List and search your collections, list and inspect flows. run Run flows you own that are marked MCP-safe. build Draft and edit flows. Nothing is ever deployed from MCP.

heading: 2. Add the server to your client
text: 2. Add the server to your client Pick your client. Then ask your assistant to run whoami to confirm the connection. Claude Code Cursor Codex Claude Desktop Other clients One command: claude mcp add --transport http raghim https://app.raghim.com/mcp \ --header "Authorization: Bearer rgh_YOUR_TOKEN" Add to ~/.cursor/mcp.json (or .cursor/mcp.json in a project): { "mcpServers": { "raghim": { "url": "https://app.raghim.com/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer rgh_YOUR_TOKEN" } } } } Then enable the server under Cursor Settings → MCP. Configuration format based on Cursor's documented remote-s

heading: 3. Tools
text: 3. Tools whoami : who the token acts as, and its scopes. list_collections , search_collection : browse and search your knowledge bases. Your client's own model writes the answer from the returned passages. list_flows , get_flow : inspect your agent flows ( get_flow includes the graph with a build-scope token). run_flow : run a flow server-side. Only flows you own and have marked MCP-safe can run, so an assistant cannot trigger a flow that sends messages or touches outside systems unless you allowed it. draft_flow , update_flow : create or edit a flow. Drafts are saved undeployed, live flows ca

heading: 4. Credits and your own OpenAI key
text: 4. Credits and your own OpenAI key On plans with credits, search costs 1 credit and flow runs and drafts use credits as in the app. Org admins can supply their own OpenAI key under Security Settings → LLM key : flow runs and drafts then use that key for generation. If the key fails, the call fails with a clear error and never falls back to the platform key. Embeddings always stay on the platform, and with your own key your prompts go to OpenAI under your account.

heading: 1. Upload your documents
text: 1. Upload your documents Sign in and open the Upload tab on the dashboard. Add your files and, if you like, type a collection name to group them. Without a name, Raghim creates a collection for you. Processing (reading, splitting and indexing the text) happens in the background, so a large file can take a few minutes before it is searchable. Scanned documents are read with OCR.

heading: 2. Manage collections
text: 2. Manage collections Open Collections to see everything you have uploaded. From there you can search collections, share one to your team, or delete one. Deleting a collection removes its documents permanently. If you upload a file directly inside the chat, it becomes a temporary collection under Chat uploads . Use Keep as collection to make it permanent, otherwise it expires.

heading: 3. Chat with your agent
text: 3. Chat with your agent Open Chat . Under Collection Selection , choose which collections the agent may use, then type your question and press Enter (Shift+Enter for a new line). Ask in English or French. Answers cite the passages they came from, so you can check them. To mix documents with database data, choose up to 3 tables under SQL Table Selection . You can speak your question with the voice button, and export an answer as a PDF. If you have a deployed flow set as active, the agent runs that flow instead of the default pipeline.

heading: 4. Put a chat widget on your website
text: 4. Put a chat widget on your website Open Widget Manager and click Create Widget , picking the collections it should answer from. Then click Get Code and paste the snippet into your site. A widget only loads on approved domains. On the hosted app, use Get Code then Request Domain Whitelisting . On a self-hosted install, your administrator adds domains to the WIDGET_DOMAINS setting.

heading: Tips
text: Tips Keep one topic per collection. Narrow collections give more focused answers. Name files clearly. Sources are shown by file name. If an answer seems wrong, check the cited sources first. The most common cause is a missing or outdated document. Previous What is Raghim? Next Your First Flow

heading: In one minute
text: In one minute Raghim lets you upload your organization's documents and data, then ask questions in plain language and get answers based on what you uploaded, with the sources shown. You can also build agent flows , which are automated assistants that search documents, query databases, send messages and hand off to people, and put a chat assistant on your website or WhatsApp. It runs as a hosted service at app.raghim.com or on your own servers, including fully offline.

heading: What you can do with it
text: What you can do with it Ask your documents Upload files and ask questions in English or French. Answers come from your documents, not from the open internet. Automate with flows Chain document search, database queries and messaging into an assistant that runs on its own. Embed a chat widget Put an assistant on your website that answers customers from your knowledge base. Connect your tools Use Raghim from code through the API, or from Claude, Cursor and Codex through MCP.

heading: Key terms
text: Key terms Collection: a named group of documents. You choose which collections the assistant may use for a question. Agent: the chat assistant. It answers from your collections and can also use database tables. Agent flow: a saved, step-by-step assistant you design on a canvas. It starts at a Start node, runs tools and logic, and ends with a reply. Widget: an embeddable chat window for your website, powered by a collection or a flow. Deploy: making a saved flow live, so the Agent and widgets use it. MCP: an open standard that lets AI tools such as Claude and Cursor connect to outside systems.
